aggressive_definition: Advanced prostate cancer; the abstract also evaluates fatal prostate cancer as a lethal endpoint
aggressive_definition_excerpt: There were 15,327 nonadvanced and 1,900 advanced prostate cancers identified through 2003 and 514 fatal cases through 2005.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: This report investigated the association between alcohol use and prostate cancer risk in a prospective cohort study of 294,707 US men aged 50-71 years in 1995-1996.
reason: The prospective cohort evaluates total incident prostate cancer and separately analyzes nonadvanced, advanced, and fatal prostate cancer. Advanced and fatal disease qualify as aggressive incident endpoints; nonadvanced disease does not.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: During follow-up, we identified 17,227 incident prostate cancer cases and further classified cases as nonadvanced (n = 15,327), advanced (n = 1,900), and fatal (n = 514).
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied full-text evidence identifies this as the all-cases incident prostate cancer estimate. It must not be relabeled aggressive merely because the article also analyzes advanced disease.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Risk of nonadvanced prostate cancer was 25% higher for men consuming ≥6 drinks daily (hazard ratio = 1.25, 95% confidence interval: 1.13, 1.37), 19% higher for men consuming 3-<6 drinks daily, and 6% higher for men consuming up to 3 drinks daily, compared with nondrinkers.
estimate_classifications.reason: The reported HR of 1.25 explicitly concerns nonadvanced prostate cancer, which is not an aggressive endpoint.

additional_estimates.comparison: Alcohol intake and advanced prostate cancer risk
additional_estimates.effect_excerpt: The authors observed no association between alcohol intake and advanced prostate cancer and an inverse association with fatal prostate cancer among heavy drinkers.
additional_estimates.count_excerpt: There were 15,327 nonadvanced and 1,900 advanced prostate cancers identified through 2003 and 514 fatal cases through 2005.
